# Link Alloy 0.0.4 — experimental alpha

This is a testing release, not a verified combined-speed improvement. Recovery hardening and sustained throughput acceptance remain incomplete. The user authorized publishing this candidate for local testing.

## Download

Download **Link Alloy Portable.exe** and run it from a writable folder as administrator. No ZIP or installer is required. The official Wintun runtime is embedded and extracted beside the executable when needed. Windows WebView2 is required. The application is unsigned; bundled driver notices are available in Settings → About & notices.

## Changes

- A fixed-window dashboard with blue/slate colors, clearer typography, visible controls and session totals. The main overview fits the tested desktop size without page scrolling.
- Network cards are paged two at a time. Every eligible link still participates in scheduling and totals, regardless of the displayed page.
- Settings is divided into Link policy, Health & logs, Diagnostics, and About & notices. Long data lists retain bounded scrolling regions and keyboard access.
- **Fixed:** a delayed UDP upstream dial could block the shared captured-packet path and stall unrelated traffic. UDP endpoint registration now precedes asynchronous dialing, with bounded admission and cancellation cleanup.
- **Fixed:** fallback dialing could reset the normal cohort rotation and bias later assignments. Retry exclusions no longer mutate that rotation.
- Regression tests reproduce both defects, verify forwarding, and check cancellation without leaking the pending UDP worker or mapping.
- Added the detailed source review and comparison with the earlier sing-box/HypoMux console setup in `docs/LOCAL_CODE_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md`.

## Known issues

- Combined throughput is not yet validated. Earlier sequential samples measured Ethernet at 94–124 Mbps, Wi-Fi at 30–31 Mbps, and a timed tunnel transfer at approximately 87 Mbps. These are historical results, not fresh measurements for 0.0.4.
- Recovery-watchdog readiness and cleanup-error handling need further hardening. Do not deliberately terminate the app or disconnect adapters as a crash/failover test with this build. Stop the tunnel normally before exiting.
- A fixed TCP half-close timeout can interrupt a legitimate remaining stream; policy writes during startup can miss the initial scheduler; flow/log failure reporting and overall dial timeouts need improvement. These are documented open findings, not fixes included in this release.
- TCP/UDP connections stay on their selected links. Equal weights do not guarantee equal bytes or full link saturation. Existing connections may reconnect when a public path changes.
- ICMP and fragmented packets remain unsupported.

## Test procedure

Stop the previous tunnel normally and close the old Link Alloy app. Fully exit the download launcher, open this executable, verify version **0.0.4**, start the tunnel, then reopen the launcher and resume the download. Compare sustained per-service download rates and bytes on both links; short pause/resume cycles can retain existing pooled sockets.

This release retains the existing alpha gates. Only the two newest published release records are kept; source tags are preserved. Assets are the portable EXE and its SHA-256 checksum file.
